bug_semantics: The OAuth callback selected an existing local account solely by the provider-returned email, retained that account's basic-auth password and signup method, linked the OAuth provider, and converted a nil EmailVerifiedAt into a verified timestamp. An attacker could therefore pre-register an unverified password account for the victim's address; the victim's later OAuth login verified and populated the same account while leaving the attacker's password usable, creating persistent account takeover.
flaw_origin: Commit 4e48320cf19e12a7195643dcbcf0360acb0821d8 added the decisive existing-account auto-verification block to server/handlers/oauth_callback.go: when the email lookup found an account with EmailVerifiedAt == nil, the callback set it to the current time. Earlier commits already matched by email and preserved the existing password, but the immediate parent still left the staged account unverified and server/resolvers/login.go rejected password login with 'email not verified'; 4e48320c first removed that gate as a side effect of the victim's OAuth callback.
ai_marker: absent: BIC commit object author and committer are both Lakhan Samani <lakhan.m.samani@gmail.com>; subject is 'fix: bug with authorizer url'; the complete commit message has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI marker
evidence: GitHub advisory API https://api.github.com/advisories/GHSA-29RF-F4VV-PVQ6 identifies CVE-2026-35511/GHSA-29rf-f4vv-pvq6, describes zero-click account takeover through OAuth linking to an unverified email account, reports vulnerable versions before pseudo-version 0.0.0-20260807033110-66fe488fd2a4, names that pseudo-version as first patched, and has withdrawn_at=null.

git diff 4e48320cf19e12a7195643dcbcf0360acb0821d8^ 4e48320cf19e12a7195643dcbcf0360acb0821d8 -- server/handlers/oauth_callback.go shows the BIC adding exactly: if user.EmailVerifiedAt == nil { now := time.Now().Unix(); user.EmailVerifiedAt = &now } in the existing-account branch after that branch preserves existingUser.Password.

Direct parent-tree verification at 34a91f3195c98069b35ddcdfd59a142d6865c63e shows server/handlers/oauth_callback.go already looked up the OAuth email, retained existingUser.Password, and updated the matched account, but contains no existing-account EmailVerifiedAt assignment; server/resolvers/login.go:42-44 rejects basic-auth login while EmailVerifiedAt is nil. Thus the complete persistent-password attack chain is absent in the immediate parent.

git cat-file commit 4e48320cf19e12a7195643dcbcf0360acb0821d8 shows the single parent 34a91f3195c98069b35ddcdfd59a142d6865c63e, human author/committer Lakhan Samani <lakhan.m.samani@gmail.com>, subject 'fix: bug with authorizer url', and no trailers or AI marker; this is a directly inspectable public commit, not a merge or identified squash aggregate.

git show 66fe488fd2a4e7acf1e517334344d5e8f3ddd296 -- internal/http_handlers/oauth_callback.go shows the direct remediation: provider-specific email-attestation results gate every path that can resolve an existing account, and replacement of an unverified pre-existing account is constrained instead of blindly linking and verifying it. Commit message explicitly identifies F1/F2 nOAuth account takeover remediation.

Tag topology: git merge-base --is-ancestor confirms 4e48320cf19e12a7195643dcbcf0360acb0821d8 is in 2.4.0-rc.15 (tag commit 7f34a65179b66034518b3e40807cb093ac4e0a72), while 66fe488fd2a4e7acf1e517334344d5e8f3ddd296 is not; the fix is an ancestor of 2.4.0-rc.16 (tag commit 3f17f68a9e0706e3b1686632ff961ac46eab1da5), matching the advisory's patched boundary and release reference https://github.com/authorizerdev/authorizer/releases/tag/2.4.0-rc.16.

CVE.org's cveawg endpoint https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-35511 returned HTTP 404 during this audit on 2026-08-30, so it supplied no contradictory rejected/withdrawn disposition; the live GitHub advisory, vendor fix commit, and release topology independently establish the vulnerability and remediation.
reasoning: The vulnerability requires three facts together: an attacker can leave a basic-auth account unverified, OAuth resolves the victim's provider identity to that row by email while retaining its password, and the callback makes the row verified so password login becomes available. History shows the linking/password-preservation mechanism predates the BIC, but the immediate parent 34a91f3195c98069b35ddcdfd59a142d6865c63e still enforces the nil verification gate. Commit 4e48320cf19e12a7195643dcbcf0360acb0821d8 is the smallest public commit that adds automatic verification of the matched existing row and therefore first completes the advisory's durable takeover chain. Commit 66fe488fd2a4e7acf1e517334344d5e8f3ddd296 directly fixes the trust-boundary error by requiring provider email attestation before existing-account resolution/linking, and the rc.15/rc.16 ancestry matches the vulnerable/patched boundary. The BIC commit object has a human author and committer and no AI marker, so later repository AI signals or the large security fix cannot attribute the origin; the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
